chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Abū Jaʿfar, from his father, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked him about the amount of water that suffices for ghusl, and he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم performed ghusl with one ṣāʿ, and performed wudu with one mudd. And the ṣāʿ in his time was five amdad, and the mudd was the measure of one riṭl and three uqiyyahs.

His statement عليه السلام in this report, that the ṣāʿ is five amdad, and the explanation of the mudd as one riṭl and three uqiyyahs, accords with the report narrated by Zurārah, because he explained the mudd as one and a half riṭls; thus the ṣāʿ comes to six riṭls, and that corresponds to this amount.

As for Sulaymān al-Marwazī’s explanation of the mudd as two hundred and eighty dirhams, it accords with the two reports, because its measure would be six riṭls by the Madinan standard. And his statement عليه السلام, five amdad, may be an error from the narrator, because what is well known from this narration is four amdad. It is also possible that this was a report about what the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to do when one of his wives shared with him in the ghusl, and that indicates this.

key_terms.أَمْدَادٍ: plural of mudd, indicating counted standard measures
key_terms.أَوَاقٍ: plural of uqiyyah, a sub-measure used in calculating the mudd
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: ghusl, the ritual bath requiring a sufficient measured amount of water
key_terms.بِصَاعٍ: with one ṣāʿ, a standard liquid measure used here for ghusl
key_terms.بِمُدٍّ: with one mudd, a smaller standard measure used here for wudu
key_terms.دِرْهَمًا: dirham, a unit used here to quantify the measure of the mudd
key_terms.رِطْلٍ: a riṭl, a weight or volume measure used to explain the mudd

ai.seo_question: How much water is sufficient for ghusl and wudu according to the hadith in al-Istibṣār?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the minimum amount of water sufficient for ghusl and wudu, relating the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and clarifying the measures of ṣāʿ and mudd. It also preserves a scholarly discussion reconciling variant reports about these measures and how they are to be understood.
